get.summary: The Lessons screen, with optional pre-game review mode
get.description: Every Lesson written on Lichess, newest first, each with its Game and that Game's Tags; Tag counts (canonical taxonomy first, then freeform) that double as the Tag filter; recurring-weakness callouts; and the Coach's Notes feed, kept separate from the user's own Lessons. The Lessons list, Tag counts, and weakness callouts honor the global filters. The `tags` and `opponent` params narrow only the Lessons list, exactly like the web's chip toggles and opponent picker. With review=true the payload also carries the pre-game review queue (the web's ?review=1 overlay), built from the whole archive and ignoring every filter, as on the web. The opponent picker options and the Coach's Notes feed are unfiltered too.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Tag names without the leading # (repeatable). Keeps only Lessons whose Game carries ALL of them, hand-written or engine-emitted alike. Omitted means no Tag restriction.

parameters.name: opponent
parameters.description: An opaque opponent ID (schema OpponentId, from GET /api/v1/opponents or lessons_opponents). Keeps only Lessons from Games against that opponent, and in review mode primes the queue with them (the web's ?review=1&opponent=X). An ID that resolves to no opponent simply matches nothing; it is not an error.

parameters.name: review
parameters.description: Mirrors the web's ?review=1: when true, the payload's review field carries the pre-game review queue; when false or omitted it is null.

LessonsPayload.description: The Lessons screen. An empty lessons list shows the web's convention explainer (write a Chapter comment starting with 'Lesson:'; add #hashtags; the canonical taxonomy chips). Source: pages/lessons.py update_lessons_page -> pgn_stats_core.lessons_table + _tag_strip -> pgn_stats_core.tag_counts (CANONICAL_TAGS); update_weakness_callouts -> pgn_stats_core.recurring_weaknesses; layout + update_lesson_opponent_options -> components.opponent_options(with_lessons_only=True); _review_overlay -> pgn_stats_core.review_queue(data.get_df()); _coach_notes_feed -> data.get_coach_notes.

games_count.description: Games after the global filters (before tags/opponent narrow the list).

lessons.description: Every Lesson after the global filters, tags, and opponent, newest first (undated last). The web's count label is this array's length.

tag_counts.description: Every Tag on the filtered Games (not narrowed by tags/opponent): canonical taxonomy Tags first in taxonomy order (only those with a count), then freeform Tags by descending count, ties by name. Each chip toggles that Tag in the `tags` param. Empty shows 'No Tags in your archive yet'.

recurring_weaknesses.description: Tags that keep showing up in recent losses, most severe first. Empty below threshold (the web then renders nothing: silence over noise).

lessons_opponents.description: The opponent picker: every named opponent the player has at least one Lesson against, across the whole archive, sorted by name.

review.description: The pre-game review queue when review=true, else null.

coach_notes.description: The Coach's Notes feed: the coach's prose on Games a Coach Study chapter matched, newest Game first, move order within a Game. Unfiltered. Empty when there is no coach content; the web then omits the feed entirely. Render it visually distinct from the user's Lessons: these are never the user's own takeaways.

LessonsLesson.description: One Lesson card. A Game with two Lessons gives two cards. The card's Tags are its Game's Tags (game.tags, with sources so engine-emitted Tags render with the muted marker).

LessonsTagCount.description: One Tag chip with its count. Not a Tag object: one Tag name aggregates both sources here, so the split is carried as counts. Each Game gives a Tag exactly one source (hand-written wins when Daniel also typed a Tag the engine emits), so count == mine_count + engine_count.

canonical.description: True for the seven taxonomy Tags; false for a freeform Tag (the web styles those differently so fragmentation stays visible).

mine_count.description: Of those, Games where the Tag is hand-written (source mine).

engine_count.description: Of those, Games where the Tag is engine-emitted (source engine). Always 0 for calculation, time-trouble, and freeform Tags.

LessonsWeakness.description: One recurring-weakness callout: a Tag on at least 3 of the last 10 Losses that also shows up in losses more than in wins and draws over the same span. Forfeits never count.

loss_count.description: How many of the windowed Losses carry the Tag.

window_losses.description: How many Losses the window holds (at most 10).

stat.description: The headline, verbatim, e.g. '#time-trouble appears in 6 of your last 8 losses'.

window.description: The months the window spans, e.g. 'Mar – Jun 2024' or 'Jun 2024'; empty when those Games are undated.

severity.description: Ranking score 0..1 (share of windowed Losses times loss association), rounded to 3 decimals. The web uses it only to order callouts.

games.description: The Losses behind the callout, in date order (any without a ChapterURL left out); the web links each as 'Game N'.

opponent_id.description: Opaque opponent ID (schema OpponentId); pass it as the `opponent` param.

LessonsReview.description: Pre-game review mode: a card-by-card walk through the most relevant Lessons, built from the whole archive (filters ignored). The client steps through cards and ends on the web's send-off ('That's everything. Now go play.'). Empty cards shows 'Nothing to review yet'.

opponent_id.description: The opponent the queue is primed with (schema OpponentId), or null when none was given or the ID resolved to no opponent.

opponent.description: That opponent's name, for the 'vs <opponent>' subtitle; null alongside opponent_id.

cards.description: Most relevant first: recurring-weakness Lessons, then Lessons against the primed opponent, then everything else; newest first within each group.

LessonsReviewCard.description: One review card: why it is in the queue, the Lesson, and its Game (opponent, outcome, date, and Tags with sources all come from game).

reason_kind.description: The queue group (review_queue priority 0, 1, 2). The web highlights recurring_weakness.

reason.description: The reason line, verbatim: 'Recurring weakness: #tactics #endgame', 'You're facing <opponent>', or 'Recent lesson'.

LessonsCoachNote.description: One Coach's Note: the coach's prose, where in the Game it was written, and the Game.

move_number.description: The 1-based full move the comment sits on; 0 for a chapter-level comment (the web shows 'before the game').
